If a Contract or Other Binding Document relates to one or more of the following, the relationship or transaction must be approved by the Board of Trustees: 3.1.1 The naming of, and name removal from, academic units, University buildings or exterior spaces (defined as those outside or upon the building envelope, streets, quads, etc.), and academic programs;

Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents Effective February 20, 2023 Page 5 of 8 3.1.2 The acquisition, transfer, disposal, or conveyance of legal title or any ownership interest in land; 3.1.3 The lease or license for use of any facility or land with an initial period great er than five (5) years and lease payments exceeding $1,000,000 over the five (5) year period; 3.1.4 The employment of any University Officer, as defined in th e Board of Trustees Bylaws; 3.1.5 Agreement with a collective bargaining unit; 3.1.6 A total financial obligation of $5 ,000,000 or more (which approval may be granted through the Board of Trustees approval of a Capital Improvement Plan or Budget if the total financial obligation is specifically identified therein), except that Board of Trustees approval is not required for orders placed under a State of Rhode Island Master Price Agreement (“MPA”) or for Contract s or Other Binding Document s through which the University agrees to participate in an MPA; 3.1.7 The settlement of a legal claim at an uninsured cost of $500,000 or more.

If a pproval by the Board of Trustees is required, all other required approvals and the approval of the President must be obtained before submission to the Board of Trustees.
When initiating a relationship or transaction that requires Board of Trustees’ approval, ample time must be allowed in the process to meet the Board of Trustees materials’ submission deadlines (information regarding those deadlines may be obtained from the Secretary to the Board of Trustees ). 3.2 President.
If a Contract or Other Binding Document relates to one or more of the following, the relationship or transaction must be approved by the President: 3.2.1 Matters requiring approval by the Board of Trustees pursuant to Section 3.1; 3.2.2 An obligation of the President established by applicable law or University policy; 3.2.3 Matters that are highly strategically important or involve potential for significant publicity; 3.2.4 A total financial obligation or exposure of $500,000 or more; 3.2.5 The settlement of a legal claim at an uninsured cost of $250,000 or more. 3.3 Vice President for Administration and Finance.

If a Contract or Other Binding Document relates to one or more of the below , the relationship or transacti on must be approved by the Vice President for Administration and Finance (VPAF) and the Contract or Other Binding Document must be reviewed and approved as specified by the VPAF.
The VPAF may designate another individual to act on their behalf with regard to the review and approval of Contracts or Other Binding Documents in accordance with internal procedures established by the VPAF. 3.3.1 Naming rights in any URI real property; 3.3.2 The purchase, sale, lease/sublease, or license/sublicense of any University interest in real property;

If a Contract or Other Binding Document relates to a one or more of the following, the relationship or transaction must be approved by the Vice President for Research and Economic Development (VPR) and the Contract or Other Binding Document must be reviewed and approved as specified by the VPR.

The Office of General Counsel must review and approve any agreement to settle or release a legal claim or dispute; any Other Binding Document relating to a legal claim or dispute; any Contract for legal services; and any Contract or Other Binding Document relating to an attorney/client relationship (including attorney/law firm engagement letters, joint representation agreements, and conflict of interest waivers).
The Office of General Counsel must also review all other Contracts and Other Binding Documents except as otherwise established in applicable Office of General Counsel protocols, processes, and procedures or where the Office of General Counsel otherwise determines that its review is not necessary. 3.6 Purchasing Department.
The Purchasing Department must review and approve all Contracts that involve the purchase or lease of goods or services, except as otherwise established in applicable Purchasing Regulations, Purchasing Department protocols , processes, and procedures or where the Purchasing Department otherwise determines that its review and/or approval is not necessary. 3.7 Office of Enterprise Risk Management.

The Office of Information Technology Services must review and approve all Contracts that involve the purchase of hardware or software, which grant a third party the right to integrate with University IT infrastructure or access campus information containing University data, or that involve third-party service providers and cloud-based vendors that provide services that process or hold institutional data, in accordance with the protocols , processes, and procedures of the Office of Information Technology Services. 4 Contract Administration; Amendments and Change Orders 4.1 Contract review and Execution is only the start of the contractual transaction or a relationship.
The Contract Owner needs to continuously evaluate whether the Contract has been satisfied, that payments have been made timely, and that the work has been completed to agreed standards and is acceptable.

If a contracting party has not performed its end of the bargain, the contracting party may be in breach of the C ontract and the University may be able to seek damages or other remedies.
If there is a potential or actual breach or a dispute about the completi on of a Contract, please contact the Office of General Counsel as soon as possible to preserve the University’s rights. 4.2 Amendments and Change Orders.
This Section applies to amendments or change orders to Contracts and Other Binding Documents originally entered into after the effective date of this policy that: (i) were approved by the Board or (ii) were not approved by the Board but would have required Board approval under Section 3 of this policy if the amendment or change order (together with any other prior amendments or change orders to the Contract or Other Binding Document) had been included at the time of approval of the original Contract. 4.2.1 Any such amendment or change order must be approved by the President , and if such amendment or change order is “material” it must also be approved by the Board.

A statute of limitations defines the period of time in which a party has to take action against another party.

President DATE: June 10, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the University of Rhode Island FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for the submission of the University of Rhode Island FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to the State of Rhode Island Department of Administration.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the enclosed University of Rhode Island FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).
Points to Consider: Every year, the University of Rhode Island submits a CIP to the State of Rhode Island.
The CIP shows capital projects of $1 million or more, in progress or proposed.

This plan is a critical and necessary step in securing funding to support the physical assets at the University and to assist with the advancement of educational and research programs that support the University’s faculty, staff, students, alumni, collaborative partners, and the citizens of the State.
The CIP identifies the projects, organizes them based on the priorities of the University, and associates a funding source with each.
The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees has two opportunities to review the proposed CIP, first at the April Board meeting as an item for review and discussion, and next at the June Board meeting for final approval and submission to the State Office of Management and Budget (OMB).
The enclosed presentation provides updates to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including: • Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 • Fine Arts Center • Athletics Complex Renewal • Biomedical Sciences Building • New University Housing • Memorial Union • Health and Counseling Center

[Type here] The CIP also includes the following new projects added since last year’s submitted FY25-FY29 CIP, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings. • Campus Accessibility • Building Envelope Improvements • Carothers HVAC Replacement • Campus Access Control • New Graduate Housing • Public Safety Building (new addition since Board consideration in April) • Automotive and Admin Services • NBC Shoreline Stabilization • New Water Tower Additionally, projects that have been removed (completed) are: • College of Engineering – Phase 2 (Bliss Hall) • Ryan Institute Lab – Phase 1 The FY2026-FY2030 CIP as recommended includes a total increase of approximately $580M. Supporting Information: Please see attached URI FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan spreadsheet and supporting presentation. Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2026- FY2030 as presented.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN FY26-FY30 Presentation to URI Board of Trustees Finance & Facilities Committee June 10, 2024

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically on July 1st. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? • There are 5 levels of approval. They are: • University of Rhode Island - Facilities Committee (internal) (April & June) • University of Rhode Island - President ’s Executive Council (March & June) • University of Rhode Island - Board of Trustees (April & June) • Executive Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July-December) • Final Approval by Governor’s Office (Third week of January) • Legislative Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) • Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects mu st be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 28% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.

New CIP Projects

New Projects: (in recommended priority order) • Campus Accessibility – This project, would provide dedicated resources to improve campus access to persons with disabilities.
Projects include restroom improvements, exterior pedestrian improvements, and discrete building improvements such as elevator modernizations.
URI has 80 elevators.
Of these, 19 are more than 30 years old and only 18 are newer than 10 years.
Many of our buildings are served by single units.
The combination of single units and aged equipment often results in downtime and limits access.
This level of support would allow for the modernization of 2-3 units per year or the replacement of one.
Funding source is RICAP - $16.5MM (FY26/27 @ $3MM FY28-30 @ $3.5MM each year) • Building Envelope Improvements – Many of the campus buildings have envelopes, including roofing systems, that are far past their serviceable life.
With water intrusion active in many locations, protecting these facilities from the damage that this causes and ensuring that environmental conditions remain safe for occupancy, this project addresses critical concerns now present on campus.

Funding source is RICAP - $53MM over 4 years • Carothers HVAC Replacement – The initial core structure of the Library was constructed in 1965 and renovated in two supplemental phases in the early ‘90s.
The current structure is 252,792 gross square feet on five floors with 175 assignable spaces.
Many air handling units are original to the building, have well exceeded their expected 30-year lifetime, and are in relatively poor condition which can adversely affect air quality.
Funding source is RICAP - $64.3MM starting in FY26 • Campus Access Control – Current evaluation of a university-wide Access Control systems is underway.
In order to provide a safer campus environment, there will be a need to update the software and hardware systems to allow for a secure campus and quick responses to emergencies such as lockdown for an active shooter event.
Total Project Cost and Schedule TBD.
Funding source is RICAP - $1.5MM (just FY26) for initial conversion to a uniform system for the campus.
Future support will be needed to tie in all buildings to this centralized system over time.

Future support level TBD • New Graduate Housing – If the Public Private Partnership does not proceed to deliver critical graduate housing, this project would replace Graduate Village and deliver 200-beds to meet the immediate need.
Based on recent market conditions, this project would require $154.1MM.
Funding source is RIHEBC in FY26

New Projects: (in recommended priority order) • Automotive & Administrative Services – To complete the creation of the new housing district on the western edge of campus and provide proper working space for Automotive and Mail & Printing Services, this project builds an addition to the Central Warehouse for Mail/Printing and provides a new Automotive repair building that replaces the current Automotive building that was once an animal barn.
Funding source is RIHEBC - $14.4MM in FY27 • Public Safety Building – The current Public Safety operations are located in three buildings, spread across the Kingston Campus, two of which are converted residential houses.
This project would combine all of these into one efficient building across from the Ryan Center.
The University Policy Department exercises full municipal-level police powers.
Police and other Public Safety personnel are the University’s first responders to situations that occur on University property while serving to promote safe practices across the community.

Funding source is RICAP - $48.3MM over 4 years starting in FY27 • NBC Shoreline Stabilization – The Bay Campus has seen significant shoreline erosion over the past 6 months as storms have intensified and hit the area directly adjacent to Pier Road, our only accessway to the new Pier.
Having already contracted with the Army Corp of Engineers, URI is looking at possible ways to secure this area so that this critical roadway is not undermined and taken out of service.
We expect that this current study will result in a $6.4MM Total Project Cost that is 35% funded with RI state funding (RICAP) ($2.24MM) and 65% federal sources ($4.16MM) • Water Tower – Built in 1971, the current water tower requires refurbishment, which will be supported by one of the Utility RIHEBC bonds.
In addition, additional water capacity is needed to support the expanding campus footprint and fire compliance needs.
Recommend building new tower after refurbishing existing tower.
Funding source is RICAP - $10.7MM over 3 years starting in FY29

The building will have four levels, each totaling 12,500 square feet. Levels 1-3 would be home to the Ryan Institute with level 1 being administrative and faculty office suites, conference rooms, and collaborative work areas and levels 2 and 3 dedicated to laboratory space. New CIP Projects

Campus Accessibility Project Statistics: • This project, would provide dedicated resources to improve campus access to persons with disabilities. Projects include restroom improvements, exterior pedestrian improvements, and discrete building improvements such as elevator modernizations. URI has 80 elevators. Of these, 19 are more than 30 years old and only 18 are newer than 10 years. Many of our buildings are served by single units. The combination of single units and aged equipment often results in downtime and limits access. This level of support would allow for the modernization of 2-3 units per year or the replacement of one. • $ 16,500,000 – RICAP • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2025 • Complete 2030 Elevator Modernization FY26 Request Accessibility Improvements

Building Envelope Improvements Project Statistics: • Many of the campus buildings have envelopes, including roofing systems, that are far past their serviceable life. With water intrusion active in many locations, protecting these facilities from the damage that this causes and ensuring that environmental conditions remain safe for occupancy, this project addresses critical concerns now present on campus. • $ 53,000,000 – RICAP • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2025 • Complete 2029 FY26 Request Ballentine Hall – College of Business 100th anniversary event Buckets throughout the lobby collecting rainwater
